title: Thy Name, Almighty Lord
description: Thy Name, Almighty Lord in Tonic Solfa to AYLESBURY, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 117, part 3.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to AYLESBURY; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thy Name, al-might-y Lord, Shall sound thro' dis-tant lands; Great is thy grace, and sure thy word, Thy truth for ev-er stands.

lines: Great is thy grace, and sure thy word,
Till morning light and evening shade

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to AYLESBURY by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
